ai.literal: not going - if there is - to me - tell - otherwise - your - quick return - to those who will live - tell
ai.translation: If you are not leaving, tell me. Otherwise, tell of your quick return to those who will still be alive.
ai.modern: நீங்கள் என்னைப் பிரிந்து செல்லமாட்டீர்கள் என்றால் அதை என்னிடம் சொல்லுங்கள். பிரிந்து சென்று விரைவில் திரும்புவீர்கள் என்றால், அதை நீங்கள் வரும்வரை உயிரோடு இருப்பவர்களிடம் சொல்லுங்கள்.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her departing lover, expressing her inability to bear the separation. She asks him to tell her only if he has decided not to leave. If he is leaving and promises a quick return, she tells him to deliver that promise to those who will survive his absence, implying she will die of grief before he returns. The contrast between 'எனக்கு உரை' (tell me) and 'வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை' (tell those who will live) powerfully conveys her certainty that she cannot survive the separation.

ai.literal: joy has-it his look separation fearing sorrow has-it indeed union
ai.translation: His look brings me joy, but our union brings me sorrow, for it makes me fear our inevitable separation.
ai.modern: அவருடைய பார்வை எனக்கு மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தருகிறது. ஆனால், அவருடனான கூடுதல், இனி வரப்போகும் பிரிவை நினைத்து அஞ்சும் துன்பத்தை எனக்குத் தருகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker contrasts the joy of her lover's gaze with the sorrow of their physical union. While his look brings pure happiness, being united with him brings distress. This is because the very act of being together makes her dread the inevitable moment he will leave again. The words 'இன்கண்' (joy) and 'புன்கண்' (sorrow) beautifully highlight the paradox of love, where the height of intimacy is shadowed by the fear of separation.

ai.literal: Difficult alas [is] consolation even from the wise, separation in one situation because of [its] reality.
ai.translation: Because separation is an undeniable reality in this situation, finding consolation is difficult, alas, even from the wise.
ai.modern: பிரிவு என்பது ஒரு நிலையில் உண்மையாக நடப்பதால், அறிவுடையவர்களால் கூட எனக்கு ஆறுதல் கூறுவது கடினமாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses the deep pain of parting from her lover. She notes that because the separation is an undeniable reality, no words of comfort can soothe her. Even the wise, who usually know how to console a grieving heart, find it difficult to offer any effective assurance in the face of this actual separation. The word 'தேற்றம்' means clarity or consolation, which is rendered impossible by the sheer fact ('உண்மையான்') of his leaving.

ai.literal: Having comforted, 'fear not', he who said, if he departs, assuring word to those who trusted, is there fault?
ai.translation: If he who comforted me and said 'fear not' departs, is it the fault of those who trusted his assuring words?
ai.modern: அன்பு செய்து 'அஞ்சாதே' என்று சொன்னவர் இப்போது பிரிந்து செல்வாரானால், அவர் சொன்ன உறுதியான சொற்களை நம்பியவர்களுக்கு ஏதாவது குற்றமுண்டோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks these words in grief when the hero, who previously promised never to leave her, departs. She recalls how he comforted her with the words 'fear not' (அஞ்சல்). She asks rhetorically if the fault lies with her for trusting his clear, assuring words (தெளித்த சொல்). The couplet highlights the pain of broken promises in love and shifts the blame from the trusting lover to the one who breaks the vow.

ai.literal: If protecting, prevent the separation of the excellent one; otherwise, if he departs, difficult indeed is union.
ai.translation: If you wish to save my life, prevent my beloved from leaving. If he departs, our reunion will be impossible.
ai.modern: என் உயிரைக் காக்க விரும்பினால், என் காதலர் என்னைப் பிரிந்து செல்வதைத் தடுத்து நிறுத்துங்கள். அவர் என்னைப் பிரிந்து சென்றால், மீண்டும் நாங்கள் ஒன்று சேர்வது கடினம்.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her friend, expressing the unbearable nature of her lover's impending departure. She says that if her friend truly wants to protect her life, she must stop him from leaving. The root word 'ōmpu' is used twice: first meaning to protect her life, and second meaning to prevent his departure. She concludes that if he does leave, a future reunion will be impossible because she will not survive the separation.

ai.translation: If he is hard-hearted enough to speak of separation, the hope that he will stay and show love is in vain.

ai.explanation: The heroine expresses her despair upon hearing her lover's plan to depart. She reasons that if he possesses the hard-heartedness to even speak of leaving her, he lacks true compassion. Therefore, any lingering hope that he might change his mind and show her love is completely unfounded. The word 'நசை' highlights her desperate desire, which is crushed by his cruel resolve.

ai.literal: Lord of the shore / fact of having forsaken / will they not proclaim / [question particle] / forearm / joint / slipping past / which are / bangles
ai.translation: Will not these bangles, slipping past the joints of my forearms, proclaim the fact that the lord of the shore has forsaken me?
ai.modern: என் முன்கையின் மூட்டுகளைத் தாண்டி நழுவி விழுகின்ற இந்த வளையல்கள், துறைவன் என்னைப் பிரிந்து சென்ற உண்மையை ஊருக்குத் தூற்றிச் சொல்லாதோ?
ai.explanation: The speaker is suffering deeply from the pain of separation. As she pines for her lover, referred to as the lord of the shore, she loses weight, causing her bangles to slip past her wrists. She wonders if these slipping bangles will not publicly proclaim the secret that he has left her. The physical symptom of slipping bangles is a classic poetic convention illustrating the physical toll of sorrow.

ai.literal: Painful is kin-without town living; even than that, painful is sweet one's separation.
ai.translation: Living in a town without any kin is painful, but parting from one's beloved is even more painful than that.
ai.modern: உறவினர் இல்லாத ஊரில் வாழ்வது துன்பமானது. ஆனால், அன்பானவரைப் பிரிந்து செல்வது அதைவிடத் துன்பமானது.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares two kinds of sorrow to emphasize the unbearable nature of parting. Living in a strange town without friends or family is a well-known hardship. However, the speaker declares that separating from a beloved partner is far more painful than that isolation. The word 'iṉiyār' refers to the sweet or dear one, highlighting the deep affection that makes the separation so agonizing.

ai.literal: If touched, it burns, except that, like the disease of love, if left, burning can it do, fire?
ai.translation: Fire burns only when touched. Can it burn when one moves away from it, like this disease of love?
ai.modern: நெருப்பு தன்னைத் தொட்டால் மட்டுமே சுடும். ஆனால் இந்தக் காதல் நோயைப் போல, தன்னை விட்டு விலகினால் நெருப்பால் சுட முடியுமா? முடியாது.
ai.explanation: The speaker contrasts the pain of love with the heat of ordinary fire. Fire only burns a person when they come into direct physical contact with it. However, the affliction of love burns the lover precisely when they are separated from their beloved. Thus, the fire of love is shown to be far more powerful and paradoxical than actual fire.

ai.literal: Difficult thing having endured, sorrowful pain having removed, separation having endured, after having stayed, they who live are many.
ai.translation: Many are those who can endure the difficulty of parting, put away their sorrowful pain, bear the separation, and live on after he has left.
ai.modern: பிரிவின் துன்பத்தைப் பொறுத்துக்கொண்டு, அதனால் வரும் துயர நோயை நீக்கி, பிரிவைத் தாங்கிக்கொண்டு காதலர் சென்ற பின்னும் உயிரோடு வாழ்பவர்கள் உலகில் பலர் இருக்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses her inability to survive her lover's departure by contrasting herself with others. She notes that there are many people who can endure the difficult moment of parting, suppress their sorrowful pain, bear the ongoing separation, and continue to live on after their lover has left. By stating that many can do this, she implies that she herself is not one of them and will not survive the separation. The repetition of the word aṟṟi (having endured) emphasizes the heavy emotional burden that others somehow manage to carry, which she finds impossible.
